A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structured-complexity-prediction work. Their text, equations, figure, algorithms and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial theoretical revisions.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, proofs and proposed applications, including phase classification, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical. Its new 50-qubit numerical example illustrates an analytical bound rather than reporting an experiment or simulation.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the shadow-based objective, Bayesian optimization and binary search. v3 makes epsilon an explicit input, replaces the 1/n acceptance threshold with epsilon, and changes the prescribed QNN sample count from LRn^4 to LRn^2/epsilon^2.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or application tasks. Quantum phase classification and circuit learning remain theoretical applications; revised formal task boundaries are covered under T1 and C1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated comparison methods. References to classical simulation and other learning approaches provide theoretical context, not baseline experiments.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to sample requirements and optimization budgets specify theoretical algorithms and guarantees, not performed evaluations.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests or evaluated case studies. The added noise analysis is a theorem and proof, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained Gaussian-process uncertainty model and probabilistic regret guarantees are theoretical.

E6.justification: v3 Section III.B adds an analytical numerical illustration: n = 50 and local depolarizing strength p = 10^-3 give a stated depth bound of 46 log(1/eta). This is a newly reported calculation, not an empirical performance improvement.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1's global-depolarizing rank argument and its supporting material in Appendix D.1–D.2. It adds Theorem 1 and Appendix E.1, deriving an expected pure/noisy-state overlap bound for general Kraus noise under independent unitary 2-design layers. It also revises SSAP and learning guarantees to explicit epsilon and logarithmic depth, and adds the coefficient-domain derivation in Appendix E.3. The local-depolarizing analysis is retained as Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the general noise–depth–purity relationship as a central contribution. The main learning guarantee narrows from O(poly log n) noisy-circuit depth in v1 Theorem 2 to O(log n) in v3 Theorem 3, while approximation accuracy becomes explicit. The central QML complexity-prediction claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive explanation for restricting pure-state approximation to logarithmic depth and interprets the new overlap bound as an applicability boundary. It also introduces a connection between circuit entanglement and noise spreading. The existing discussions of sampling advantages and prospective applications largely remain.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix D.4 supplies coarse coefficient-domain intervals. v3 Appendix E.3 additionally describes estimating their bounds through one-dimensional polynomial optimization, including kernel choices and approximation margins. This provides more explicit computational instructions without demonstrating a new implementation.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Cerezo et al. cost-dependent barren-plateau reference and Anschuetz–Kiani traps reference from v1. It expands the introduction's discussion of Gibbs-ball simulation limits and AdS/CFT motivation using existing references. Appendix A's principal research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Existing passages in the introduction, noise setup, task statement and algorithm exposition are substantially rewritten. Section III is reorganized, Section IV gains a Metric Construction subsection, and the proof appendices are restructured. These changes recast the narrative beyond theorem renumbering; authorship and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to identify the noisy-state shadow, show N sampled QNN circuits and label the loss connecting them. Its three-panel organization remains. Algorithm blocks shift within the layout, but no experimental plots or result tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: The explicit error-dependent algorithms and new coefficient-domain construction make the method easier to assess, while Theorem 1 supplies a conditional noise–depth characterization absent from v1. These are useful gains in specificity. However, the new theorem is ensemble-averaged, and Section VI.B and Appendix A retain polylogarithmic scope wording despite Theorem 3's logarithmic restriction, limiting the improvement in overall clarity and rigor.
